agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby to review Pender St. traffic calming petition
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a petition signed by 86 residents requesting permanent traffic calming on Pender Street and adjacent streets in North Burnaby, from Boundary Road eastward. The request follows a fatal pedestrian collision at Pender and MacDonald on August 10, 2026. Staff will review road safety options, including speed humps, enhanced crosswalks, one-way diverters and curb bulges, and work with the RCMP on enforcing stop signs and speed limits. This is a proposal under consideration, not a final decision.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you drive or own a business on Pender Street or adjacent North Burnaby streets, watch for updates on this review and any future public consultation.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider road safety review for Lougheed Town Centre
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a staff review of road safety concerns in the Lougheed Town Centre area. The proposal follows a report from residents about traffic issues, including a request for a 'No right turn on red' restriction at Grande Promenade and Austin Rd. City staff would look at specific locations to see if more safety improvements can be made, and would coordinate enforcement of traffic violations with Burnaby RCMP and Bylaw Enforcement. This is a proposed step, not a final decision — Council will vote on whether to direct staff to proceed with the review.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you operate a business in the Lougheed Town Centre area, watch for the Council decision and any future public consultation on road changes.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: MacPherson Outdoor Pool correspondence sent to Parks Committee
agenda_briefs.summary: Council is set to consider correspondence from Anna Hittrich about the MacPherson Outdoor Pool. The item has been referred to the Parks, Recreation and Culture Committee for review. This is a proposed step, not a final decision. The correspondence urges the reopening of the pool next summer, noting it has been closed for years due to leaks and repairs. The committee will look into the matter and may bring forward recommendations at a future council meeting. Business owners and community members who use or rely on the pool should watch for upcoming committee discussions and any potential changes to pool operations or hours.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for Parks Committee meeting dates and any public input opportunities regarding the MacPherson Outdoor Pool.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Montecito Park dog park conversion referred to Parks Committee
agenda_briefs.summary: Council is set to consider a proposal to convert an underutilized area of Montecito Park into a designated off-leash dog park. The proposal, submitted by Burnaby resident Mehdi Joharchi of 7315 Montecito Dr., has been referred to the Parks, Recreation and Culture Committee for review. If approved, the fenced, signed area with waste disposal stations would create a new off-leash space for dogs in Burnaby. The decision is still pending and has not been finalized.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Parks Committee meeting date and attend to voice your support or concerns about the proposed dog park.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider urban Canada goose management pilot
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a request for a one-year Urban Canada Goose Management Pilot in Burnaby's highest-conflict parks, referred to the Parks, Recreation and Culture Committee. If approved, the pilot could include a federally permitted egg-addling and nest-monitoring program, a public nest-reporting system, habitat changes, humane hazing, and improved feeding enforcement. Businesses with outdoor spaces like parks, golf courses, and other goose-affected properties may be impacted. No changes are in effect yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Parks Committee meeting date and consider attending to share your views.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby Council to refer 'Safer Streets in the Heights' to Public Safety Committee
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider referring a correspondence item called 'Safer Streets in the Heights' to the Public Safety Committee. The correspondence, submitted by resident Sophia Oblitas Van Straten, documents crashes, injuries, and deaths along Albert St., Hastings St., and Pender St. in North Burnaby (The Heights) over the past 3 years, citing speeding and impatient drivers as leading causes. If referred, the committee would review the matter and could recommend future actions, but no changes are in effect yet. Business owners in the area may want to monitor this as it could lead to future traffic or public safety measures.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Monitor council's decision on this referral—it could lead to future street safety changes affecting your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Metro Vancouver Board to consider July 24, 2026 agenda items
agenda_briefs.summary: The Metro Vancouver Board accepted the City of New Westminster's and District of North Vancouver's Regional Context Statements, aligning their Official Community Plans with the Metro 2050 regional growth strategy. The Board deferred a report estimating $114.8 billion in infrastructure investment is needed over the next 15 years to support approximately 570,000 new homes by 2041, equating to $201,000 per new home ($74,000 from member jurisdictions, $26,000 from Metro Vancouver).
agenda_briefs.action_required: Monitor Metro Vancouver for the deferred infrastructure funding report and future updates to New Westminster's Official Community Plan and growth targets.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Metro Vancouver Housing Data Dashboard launch and 2026 update
agenda_briefs.summary: Metro Vancouver launched its new online Housing Data Dashboard on June 26, 2026, replacing the hard-copy Housing Data Book. The dashboard consolidates regional and municipal housing data into six thematic areas with 32 topic pages and 132 visualizations, refreshed throughout the year. The 2026 update shows housing starts fell to 27,185 in 2025, completions hit a record 30,855 units, and median purpose-built rents rose 3% to $1,875.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Review the dashboard's 2026 data on housing starts, completions, and rents to inform your business location and workforce decisions.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider LGCAP funding response from BC Ministry
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a response from the BC Ministry of Energy and Climate Solutions regarding funding for the Local Government Climate Action Program (LGCAP). The Ministry confirms current LGCAP funding is secured through March 31, 2027, and that options for the program's future are being considered as part of the Budget 2027 process. This is an information item for Council — no decision has been made yet. The outcome could affect how the City funds climate action programs, which may impact local businesses through future fees or programs.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Monitor the Council decision — funding changes could affect future climate-related fees or programs for your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: New Westminster letter on North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant
agenda_briefs.summary: New Westminster City Council has formally requested that the Inspector of Municipalities conduct an independent review under Section 765 of the Local Government Act into Metro Vancouver governance and the North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant project. The review would examine governance, oversight, procurement, financial management, and decision-making for the project. The letter was sent August 12, 2026, following a July 13, 2026 council resolution supporting Surrey's efforts for greater transparency and accountability.
agenda_briefs.action_required: No action needed from business owners at this time. Monitor the review outcome if your business is affected by wastewater infrastructure.

agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider signing support letters for the Local Government Climate Action Program (LGCAP) funding applications from the City of Salmon Arm and the Village of Slocan. This is a proposed item on the agenda — no decision has been made yet. If approved, Burnaby would formally back these communities' requests for provincial climate action funding. The letters are part of a routine intergovernmental support process and would not directly impose new rules or costs on Burnaby businesses.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby to consider anti-human trafficking initiative at UBCM
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a report on an anti-human trafficking initiative presented at the UBCM Trade Booth 522. The proposal, brought forward by Cathy Peters, aims to raise awareness and address human trafficking. It calls for four strategies in BC: a provincial educational campaign, updating provincial police policies to align with the federal Protection of Communities and Exploited Persons Act (PCEPA), education for crown counsel and the judiciary, and school education. Council is set to review the initiative and decide whether to support or adopt any related measures. This is a proposed action, not yet approved.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Monitor council discussions and the UBCM report for any new requirements that could affect your business operations.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby 'Density Without Demolition' framework under review
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider correspondence from Linda Jeaurond urging Burnaby to pass a resolution matching Qualicum Beach's July 15, 2026 motion calling on the Province to modernize the BC Building Code for adaptive reuse and internal home conversions. The framework would unlock existing floor space — from under-utilized homes to vacant commercial properties — to add density without demolition. The correspondence notes the Fall 2026 BC Building Code update still restricts exemptions for existing buildings to projects with zero structural alterations, and cites Clean Energy Canada analysis showing lower-carbon design cuts embodied emissions by 30% and construction costs by 12% in multi-unit projects.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Monitor council updates on this framework — it could affect future development or renovation plans.

Gregorowicz asks Council to direct staff to produce a complete report of every permit and application still in-stream or under construction. This is a proposed discussion item, not a final decision.
